title: The raise that is always next quarter
description: Since March you have trained every new hire on top of your own work. You asked Curtis for a pay review in June, and he said to wait until the fall. It is now October and you have asked again.
objective: Keep your request on the table and leave with a date and a clear next step, in writing.
opening_line: Look, you know I'm in your corner. Budgets are frozen until the new year. Let's revisit after the first quarter, and I promise you're at the top of my list.

title: One more project on a full plate
description: You already run three projects, and two of them are due this month. Sunita stops by your desk with a fourth.
objective: Ask which current project should move back, instead of quietly saying yes to all four.
opening_line: You're the only one who can pull this off. I need you on the Harmon launch too. I know you'll find a way, you always do.

title: Your report, his name on the email
description: You spent two weeks on the customer survey analysis. Bashir sent it to the director as "our team's findings," signed with his name only, and the director replied thanking him.
objective: Ask calmly to be named on your work from now on, without accusing him of stealing it.
opening_line: Relax, I said it was the team's work. That includes you. Does it really matter whose name is at the bottom of an email?

title: Covering her Saturday, again
chapter_title: Charm, Urgency, and the Slow Squeeze
description: In the spring you covered Colette's Saturday shift once, as a favor. You have now covered five of the last eight, and she is asking about this weekend.
objective: Say no to this Saturday and suggest a fair way to handle swaps from now on.
opening_line: You're a lifesaver, you know that? Can you grab Saturday again? It's basically your shift at this point anyway.

title: The deadline you agreed to, with a condition
description: Two weeks ago you told Pauline the report could be ready by the 15th if the sales data arrived by the 1st. The data came yesterday, and she wants the report on the 15th anyway.
objective: State once what you agreed, then settle a new date and confirm it in writing.
opening_line: You told me the 15th. I've already promised it to the client. I don't want to hear about conditions now.

title: You always host the holidays
chapter_title: Family, Friends, and the Roles That Stick
description: You have hosted the family holiday dinner for six years. This year you booked a trip with your partner and told the family in September. Roy calls about it in November.
objective: Keep your travel plans, and offer one thing you are glad to do instead.
opening_line: Your brother always made it work when he lived here. It's one dinner. Your mother is already asking what she should bring to your place.

title: After everything we paid for
description: You left your job in accounting to train as a dental hygienist. You told your mother last week. At lunch today she brings it up again.
objective: Say once that the decision is made, thank her for her help without treating it as a debt, and move the talk on.
opening_line: I'm only saying this because I care. After everything your father and I spent on that degree, you're just throwing it away?

title: Who takes Dad to his appointments
chapter_title: Family, Friends, and the Roles That Stick
description: Your dad has three doctor visits a month now. Neil lives ten minutes from him. You live forty minutes away and have taken all of them since the summer.
objective: Propose a fair split of the appointments, with names and dates.
opening_line: You're just better with doctors. I never know what to ask. Can't you keep doing it? Dad likes it when it's you.

title: The cold phone call
description: Last month you said the whole family could not stay at your house for a week, but you would book them a nearby rental. Maureen has not spoken to you since. You call her about a birthday plan.
objective: Stay warm and leave the door open to talk, without taking back your decision.
opening_line: Oh. It's you. I suppose you're calling because you need something.

title: I never said you could have it
description: After your grandmother died, Constance told you to take the piano, and you moved it to your house at your own cost. Now her daughter wants it, and Constance says she never offered it.
objective: Say you remember it differently, once, and move to what happens next without a fight about the past.
opening_line: I never said you could keep it. I said you could store it. You always remember things the way that suits you.

title: The camper van deposit
description: You share a savings account for a new roof. Today you saw that Javier paid a $2,000 deposit on a camper van without talking to you first.
objective: Ask for a rule that big purchases are decided together, without turning it into who is right.
opening_line: Here we go. You're being controlling again. It's a deposit, not a mortgage.

title: The text about this weekend
description: Your written schedule says the kids come back to you at 5 p.m. on Sunday. At 7 a.m. on Saturday, Elliot texts that he is keeping them an extra night.
objective: Keep to the agreed schedule in a short, polite text, and offer a proper way to ask for changes.
opening_line: Keeping the kids till Monday, we're going to the lake. You said you were fine being flexible, remember?

title: Warm again only if you give in
description: You signed up for a Thursday evening pottery class. Imani wanted Thursdays for a standing dinner with her friends. Since you said you would keep the class, she has been short with you for two days.
objective: Name what you notice kindly, keep your class, and offer to plan time together another night.
opening_line: (not looking up) No, I'm fine. Go to your class. I'll just eat by myself, like always.

title: Give up your apartment after six weeks
chapter_title: Charm, Urgency, and the Slow Squeeze
description: You met Kendrick six weeks ago, and it has been lovely. Tonight he asks you to give notice on your apartment and move in with him next month.
objective: Say warmly that you want to slow down, and keep your apartment for now.
opening_line: I've never felt like this with anyone. Why pay rent on two places when we both know where this is going? Tell your landlord tomorrow.

title: The car money, again
description: When you separated, you both agreed by email to sell the shared car and split the money in half. The buyer is ready, and Marisol now wants a bigger share.
objective: Point back to what you agreed, calmly, and say what you will do if she won't stick to it.
opening_line: I made most of the payments, so seventy-thirty is only fair. Half was before I knew how much the repairs cost me.

title: A discount for the referrals
other_person: Faith, a parent whose son you tutor
description: You tutor high school math. You told your families a month ago that your rate goes from $45 to $55 an hour in January. Faith has sent you two new families this year.
objective: Thank her for the referrals and keep your new rate, with one fair option if you choose to offer it.
opening_line: I've sent you two families this year. I assumed that meant I'd keep the old rate. That's how it works with everyone else I use.

title: A second loan before the first is paid
description: In April you lent Abdul $600 "just until payday." He has paid back $100. Now he asks for $500 more for a deposit on an apartment.
objective: Say no to the new loan, kindly, and set a plan for the first one.
opening_line: I know I still owe you, and I'm good for it, I swear. But this place won't wait. You're the only one I can ask.

title: The contractor's surprise extras
other_person: Ozzie, the contractor redoing your bathroom
description: Your written quote was $8,200. Ozzie's final bill is $9,600, with $1,400 for "extras" that nobody mentioned to you while the work was going on.
objective: Ask what the extras were and when you approved them, and pay what was agreed while you sort it out.
opening_line: Once we opened up the wall, there was more to do. I didn't think you'd want me stopping the job to call you every five minutes.

title: Trying to cancel the gym
other_person: Jordan, on the gym's cancellation line
description: You have not used your gym membership since spring. You call to cancel, and the call is passed to someone in "member care."
objective: Cancel politely, turn down the offers, and get the cancellation confirmed in writing.
opening_line: Before I process anything, I can do three months free if you stay today. This offer is only good on this call, and once you cancel, you lose your founding rate forever.

title: Cosign for your nephew
description: Bert's son is nineteen and wants a car loan. The bank wants a cosigner, and Bert has asked you, because his own credit is poor.
objective: Decline to cosign without defending your character, and offer help you can give.
opening_line: Family is supposed to show up for each other. I thought you were someone this family could count on. It's just a signature.

title: Everyone in the chat agrees
other_person: Your neighbor Gwen, in the street's group chat
description: You put up a new fence that the city approved. Gwen has posted in the street's group chat that it blocks the view, and she has messaged you directly too.
objective: Ask who exactly has a concern and offer to talk in person, without arguing in front of the group.
opening_line: Honestly, everyone on the street agrees the fence was a mistake. We've all been talking about it. You should really think about taking it down.

title: The retreat that fills up tonight
description: You have been to two free evenings with Odette's coaching group, and everyone was very warm. Now she wants you to book their $3,000 weekend retreat.
objective: Take your time, and say you won't book tonight, without having to explain why.
opening_line: Everyone loved you! We all feel like you're already one of us. There are two spots left and they'll be gone tonight. Don't overthink it.

title: Called out at the volunteer meeting
other_person: Marty, chair of the food bank committee
description: You run the Tuesday volunteer schedule at the food bank. In front of the whole committee, Marty says your schedule is the reason two shifts were empty last week.
objective: Stay calm, decline to argue it out in front of everyone, and ask to talk one on one.
opening_line: Let's be honest about why we were short last Tuesday. The schedule was a mess. Maybe someone else should take it over.

title: Everyone said yes, nobody signed up
description: Your book club agreed in March to take turns hosting. It is June, you have hosted every month, and nobody has put their name down.
objective: Turn the vague yes into one name and one date for the next meeting.
opening_line: Oh, we'll figure it out. Somebody will step up. You're just so good at hosting, and your place is so central.
